input.question: what and why is mixing and mastering (music) good for?
input.ground_truth: For a more ELI5 answer: Think about an awesome sandwich. Any person can put a bunch of great ingredients in and it'll taste fine, but what makes a great sandwich is putting the right ingredients with the right amounts of each. Too much mustard and even if there are other things you still have a mustard sandwich, too little and the sandwich is missing something. For your second question: not always. Some people are great at making a sandwich(composer), some people can taste what else the sandwich needs or how to rearrange it better(producer/sound tech/arranger/orchestrator - yes all of these roles can change a piece) some people can do both, some people can't do either. Edit: first example was a producer/sound tech. Here's others Placement of the ingredients: orchestrator. This is for a live Sound btw. Arranger: the main ingredient (melody) tastes great. Keep that, but change the other ingredients (harmonies, chords, counter-melodies. Source - Classically trained musician.

Okay! Imagine you made a big bowl of soup with lots of different veggies and noodles. But right now, some veggies are too loud and you can’t taste the noodles.

Mixing is like stirring the soup so all the pieces are together and you can taste everything nicely.  
Mastering is like tasting the soup and making it just the right amount of salty, spicy, and yummy so it sounds great on every spoon (or speaker).

So, mixing and mastering help your music sound clear, balanced, and really nice for everyone who listens!
